title: Week 9 Preview: Philly Can Punch His Ticket, Kai Faces the Team He Traded With, and Brucie Gets a Green Bay Problem
dek: Team Pillbert can all but clinch against the manager who owns him, the trade partners meet in a must-win, and Sonny tries to steady a lineup that swings like a pendulum.
body: The marquee game is a case of the hot team against the team that has history on its side. Habibsters have won three straight, with the last two at 119.84 and 120.96, and Habib holds a 7-2 edge over Philly in this series. The catch is that one of those two losses came in Week 2, a 135.48 to 109.66 beating, and Team Pillbert hasn't slowed down much since. Luffy gives Kaushal a 42% chance, and the stakes are lopsided: a win all but seals Alan's playoff spot, while Habib's win would move him toward safety and a loss would leave his season hanging on a coin flip. Jahmyr Gibbs and Puka Nacua are the players who decide this one, and the quarterback duel is waiver-wire find Drake Maye against Brock Purdy.

Then there's the trade rematch. The fumblers and Dawgs swapped Tee Higgins and Jameson Williams for Jonathan Taylor and Amon-Ra St. Brown, and Higgins and Williams both start for Randy this week against the team that sent them over. Kai answers with Taylor in a backfield next to James Cook III, and has enough depth that St. Brown isn't even in his starting lineup. The series is tied 6-6, and Luffy gives Randy a 22% chance to end his five-game losing streak. That losing streak has also put his whole season on the line, because a loss leaves The fumblers close to finished, while a win keeps them breathing. Brock Bowers and Derrick Henry are the players to watch.

No Banner only HULK lost by 0.92 last week and still leads the league in points by a mile, which is how Brucie loses: angrily, and with a scoreboard that says he deserved better. His opponent, Ghostu-Spider SZN, comes in at 3-5 with Jared Goff under center and an A.J. Brown spot to sort out before Sunday. The fun subplot is a Green Bay standoff, with Packers rookie Matthew Golden in Ramon's lineup and Tucker Kraft in Zoe's. Luffy gives Z² a 20% chance, and Kenneth Walker III against Bijan Robinson is the matchup that settles it. A loss for Zoey leaves her playoff hopes on fumes, while a win would put her back in the conversation.

Finally, The Horse is Hea plays Counting or not Counting GV, which looks like the safest game of the week until you look at Sonny's recent scores: 102.58, 146.72, then 73.5. Ashton Jeanty, now on his third roster since Week 5, starts in Sonny's backfield, and George Kittle is the player who most likely decides whether this is a stroll or a sweat. JMoney arrives off the week-high 138.28 with Joe Burrow, who threw him a party last Sunday and needs another one. Luffy gives Sonny a 75% chance, Sonny won the Week 2 meeting by 60, and a win keeps him comfortably in the top four. A loss would make the next few weeks a lot more stressful. Watch Parker Washington too, a quiet WR2 on Sonny's side who could swing a close one.

social.author: Sal Benedetto
social.text: Habibsters is a LOCK. Dawgs is a LOCK. HULK is a LOCK. And Counting or not Counting GV is a LOCK because The Horse is Hea owes me. Write it down. Frame it.

social.author: Pillbert Til I Die
social.text: Marcus Pell says the 7-2 series record matters more than what happened in Week 2. Respectfully, Week 2 was 135 to 109. We are not the same team we were in 2024, Marcus.

social.author: Dr. Nina Kessler
social.text: My Week 9 card is all chalk except none. Philly, Sonny, Ramon, Kai. If you want to fade Luffy this week, the one spot I'd consider is Puka Nacua going 28-plus for Habib. That gets Habibsters to 63%.

social.author: Fumble Recovery Unit
social.text: Marcus Pell is the only person on the panel picking us and he went 1-3 last week. I'll take it. Revenge game for Higgins. Somebody believes. Barely.

social.author: Gamma Ray Gang
social.text: Marcus picking Ghostu-Spider SZN over us for the second week in a row is the most stubborn thing I've seen since Randy's roster. HULK by 30.

social.author: Horse Sense
social.text: Sal picked JMoney over us because WE owe HIM. Sal, we don't know you. Kittle is coming for your whole bankroll.

social.author: Habibsters
social.text: Matchday. Three straight wins, Puka and CeeDee up top, and a Team Pillbert side waiting. Let's make it four. #HabibNation

panel.take: Habib's lineup is healthy and hot, but Philly has three running backs who all start and get the ball. I'm also hearing Luther Burden III is the sleeper here; nobody on Habib's side is planning for him.
Seven wins in nine meetings is not a coincidence, it's a hierarchy. Week 2 was the exception, and three straight wins say Kaushal is ready to restore the order of things.
Habibsters cashed for me last week and I don't abandon a winner. LOCK. Puka eats.
Luffy has Team Pillbert at 58%, and Gibbs is the reason: if he gets to 34 points, Philly jumps to 79%. Habib needs Puka at 28 or more just to get to 63%.

picks.game: The Horse is Hea (Sonny) vs Counting or not Counting GV (Jordan)

panel.take: Sonny has the deeper lineup by a lot and Jeanty gets another shot in his backfield. Burrow can keep it close, but he can't be the whole team twice in a row.
Champions don't lose two out of three to a 2-6 team in November. Sonny remembers 73.5 and so does everyone else, which is exactly why he answers this week.
The Horse is Hea burned me last week and I have a long memory. Burrow throws for 40 again. LOCK, and I'm not explaining myself.
Luffy has Sonny at 75%, and Kittle at 21 or more pushes that to 90%. Even if Burrow hits 27, JMoney only gets to 41%; that's not enough to fade.

picks.game: Ghostu-Spider SZN (Zoe) vs No Banner only HULK (Ramon)

panel.take: Zoe has a spot to fill before Sunday and Ramon doesn't. Walker, Swift and Allen is too much firepower.
Yes, I picked her last week and missed. The rookie keeps getting closer, and the Hulk just lost to a bench full of points. Upsets come when you stop expecting them.
Lost by less than a point last week and still the best team in this league. Brucie is MAD. LOCK.
Luffy says 80% for Ramon, and a 29-point Walker game makes it 94%. Zoe's path is Bijan at 23 or more, and even then it's only 35%.
Taylor and Cook both start, and Kai can leave St. Brown on the bench. That's the clearest sign of which side won the trade.
Six to six all time, and Tee Higgins gets to play the team that left 32 points on its bench. Revenge is the oldest storyline in sports, and Randy needs one.
The fumblers burned me last week too. Not again. Dawgs, LOCK, and Marcus can keep his revenge storyline.
Luffy has Dawgs at 78%, and Bowers at 23 or more makes it 91%. Randy needs 19 or more from Henry just to get to 37%.
